newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedbank Q1 profit boosted by commission.
newsitem.headline: Swedbank Q1 profit boosted by commission.

text.p: Swedish bank Swedbank on Wednesday reported a nine percent rise in operating profit to 1.32 billion crowns ($172.3 million) due to higher net commission revenue, lower costs and reduced loan losses.

"Swedbank has made a better first quarter than last year in spite of the fact that this year there was no comparable decline in long-term interest rates as in the first quarter of 1996," chief executive Reinhold Geijer said in a results statement.

"Substantially higher commission income from, among other things, fund and insurance savings, compensated for the decrease in net income from financial operations and expenses have decreased," he added.
Swedbank, which intends to merge with Foreningsbanken, said net commission rose 33 percent to 792 million crowns in the first three months of the year from the corresponding quarter last year.
Total costs fell to 2.12 billion crowns from 2.19 billion and loan losses declined to 300 million crowns from 460 million crowns for a fall in loan loss ratio to 0.3 percent from 0.5.
Net interest income was little changed at 2.41 billion crowns compared to 2.40 billion.
"Net interest income is unchanged although the governmental charge for deposit guarantee has doubled from last year," Geijer added.
Both lending and savings rose and earnings per share increased to 3.36 crowns from 3.10.
The capital adequacy ratio was 12.4 percent at the end of the first quarter, compared to 11.8 percent a year earlier.

On the negative side, the bank noted that total income fell three percent to 3.73 billion crowns following lower net income from financial operations after a decline in long-term interest rates boosted 1996 figures.
Net income from financial operations dropped to 117 million crowns from 479 million.
-- Birgitta Forsberg, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1006 ($ = 7.661 Swedish Crowns)
